rv.q: Exton’s stop-go plotting and the sagging patches in Harry Burton’s production prevent the material from developing any comic momentum.
But to me it felt a terrible waste of a strong cast.
I incline to the view that this is because it isn’t much good.
But what should be played as fast-moving farce feels much longer than its two-and-a-quarter hours, and even the swearing becomes tiresome after a while.
It's just irredeemably and gloriously bad.

cn.t: Critics find this posthumous Clive Exton comedy desperately unfunny despite its star cast. The foul-mouthed Essex crime farce suffers from stop-go plotting, lacks comic momentum, and relies on crude mockery over genuine wit.
